claim: The entry-level pain is EADDRINUSE plus forgotten lsof flags: users repeatedly say they google the lsof command every time and want one obvious place/command to see and kill what's on a port.
quote: i get tired of spamming lsof -i tcp:xxxx / I always forget the lsof flags and end up googling them every time
title: Show HN: Sonar - A tiny CLI to see and kill whatever's running on localhost

claim: Orphaned dev servers from old worktrees, cross-project port blocking, and forgotten Docker containers are the author's stated motivation for sonar - a multi-server management gap, not just single-port killing.
quote: A big pain of mine was constantly running into port: Redis from one project blocking another, orphaned dev servers from old worktrees, Docker containers I forgot about.
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Sonar's launch was the breakout in this category: 204 points / 77 comments on HN, while ~15 near-identical macOS menu-bar port apps (Pscan, Portsly, PortPilot, Switchboard, p0rt, OpenPorts, PortManager...) each got 1-60 points, mostly under 5.
quote: 204 points by raskrebs | 77 comments
location: HN item stats + algolia search results
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: A top-asked surface is a tray/menubar GUI on top of the CLI data - requested on HN ('run in the system tray'), filed as sonar issues #15 ('Create a MacOS app') and #21 ('Add tray to linux'), and shipped as 'Open Ports in Menu Bar' in Raycast Port Manager.
quote: Would be cool if it could run in the system tray and show what's running on your ports at a glance.
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Users ask for a 'next free port' command because the try-fail-hunt-retry loop is the daily EADDRINUSE workflow; filed and shipped as sonar issue #5/#12 ('sonar next: find the next available port').
quote: EADDRINUSE is a common problem. The typical workflow is: try to start a service, it fails, manually hunt for a free port, update your config, try again. There's no standard, fast CLI command to just answer 'what port can I use?'
title: [Feature] sonar next: find the next available port

claim: Port-readiness gating is a requested feature: 'sonar wait' blocks until a port accepts connections with --http readiness checks and timeouts (issues #6/#13); the author also planned 'wait for a host to return a successful health check before proceeding - good for migrations'.
quote: wait (wait for a host to return a successful health check before proceeding - good for migrations
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Notifications on server lifecycle are an explicit want: new/unknown server appearing (Rungeist markets 'menu-bar icon lights up the moment an unfamiliar server starts listening'), port owner changes (Porticle 'notifies when their owner changes'), and crash/exit notification with optional relaunch (HN user built this in Keyboard Maestro).
quote: I manually set something up in Keyboard Maestro to notify me that something quit and potentially re-launch it.
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Project attribution ('which project does this port belong to') is the core differentiator users respond to - every serious tool resolves cwd->project (package.json/pyproject/Cargo/go.mod/.git), and HN Switchboard's one comment asks for favicon+title detail to identify servers.
quote: Would be awesome to get more details about what's running on ports like the favicon if it's a website running with its name and some other details
location: HN comment (mfbz) on Switchboard Show HN
title: Show HN: Switchboard - Mac menu bar app that shows every localhost port

claim: AI-agent-started servers are a 2026-emergent complaint and now a marketed feature axis: agent attribution ('who started it' - Claude Code/Codex/Cursor logos in Portkeeper, session linking in Roulette) and agent cleanup ('Your agent left servers everywhere. Clean up in one.' on rungeist.com).
quote: Your AI agent spins up a dev server and moves on. You never see it, but Rungeist does
title: Rungeist - every dev server and port on your Mac

claim: Claude Code leaves background dev servers running after session transitions/end; a user measured one orphaned workerd at 89% CPU and 2.5GB RAM over 2 days (issue #16198).
quote: This results in orphaned processes consuming significant resources (in my case, 89% CPU and 2.5GB RAM over 2 days).
title: Background dev servers not cleaned up when session transitions to new tasks

claim: Orphaned agent processes accumulate under parallel-agent/worktree workflows and create memory pressure; users report 3+ orphans surviving a weekend and '8+ GB' orphaned next dev servers (claude-code #27959, #43944).
quote: With multiple Claude Code sessions (worktree workflow), orphans accumulate fast. On a 16GB machine running 4-6 Claude Code instances, this contributes to memory pressure and swap thrashing
title: Background bash commands become orphan processes after session close or task interruption

claim: On Windows the orphan problem is measurably worse: no cascading process-tree kill and PID reuse mean dead parents' children persist; one report: 11 orphaned git-bash + 7 node processes that even blocked the Git for Windows installer (claude-code #77593); another: 25+ node + 14+ bash orphans at 85% CPU/73% memory (#41742).
quote: Because Windows has no cascading process-tree kill, the children keep running indefinitely after their parent bash.exe/node dies. ... 11 orphaned Git-Bash processes ... + 7 orphaned node processes accumulated. The Git for Windows installer refused to proceed
title: Windows: background Bash tool processes orphaned across sessions

claim: Windows orphans are invisible in stock tooling: Task Manager cannot show project/session for them - 'an orphan shows up as one more top-level node.exe'.
quote: Task Manager's tree only nests a process under a parent that's still alive, so an orphan shows up as one more top-level node.exe.
title: Finding the processes Claude Code leaves running on Windows

claim: Windows demand is expressed by building, not just asking: DevBar exists explicitly as a Windows counterpart to a macOS-only tool; Sweepling was written because cc-reaper is macOS/Linux only; sonar got a community PR 'Add Windows support' (#17) merged with netstat/CIM/taskkill equivalents.
quote: A Windows counterpart to backquant/mac-devbar, rebuilt natively in C#/WPF with the Windows-specific tools a dev box actually needs.
title: DevBar for Windows

claim: Newer cross-platform entrants treat Windows as first-class: Porticle ships 'macOS 13+ / Windows 10+' system tray; Roulette (Tauri) covers macOS/Windows/Linux; portcheck-tray ships Windows+Linux builds; marcellosso/localhost needed 'shared core over a named pipe' specifically for Windows. The macOS-only crowd (Rungeist, pier, Portsmith, Kiri-app) is the older pattern.
quote: A fast, open-source menu bar and system tray app for seeing—and stopping—what is using your local ports. macOS 13+ · Windows 10+
title: Porticle

claim: Safe-kill is a repeated hard requirement, not a nicety: users want confirmation + process-group kills (agents spawn shell->npm->CLI->server chains where stopping the port owner leaves the rest), PID-reuse re-validation, protect-lists (databases/OS), and verified death (Force Kill fallback).
quote: Agent-started servers are usually a chain: a shell, npm, the framework CLI, then the server itself. Stopping the process on the port can leave the rest. Stop the whole process group.
title: Claude Code left a dev server running?

claim: 'Kill parent, not just listener' is a real ask because watchers (nodemon etc.) respawn the server - Raycast Port Manager ships 'Kill Parent'; Porticle detects 'ports that reopen under a supervisor'.
quote: Kill Parent (⌥ ⌘ P) stops the process that started the listener. That's the one you want when nodemon or a watcher keeps bringing the server back.
title: Find and Kill the Process Using a Port on Mac

claim: The 'forgotten/zombie server' concept has a de-facto shared spec across tools: flag when terminal/parent gone, project folder deleted, a newer duplicate of the same server is running, or uptime >1 day - and never flag databases/Docker/OS services (protect classes).
quote: its terminal is gone: the shell that started it exited and it got re-parented to init/launchd; its folder was deleted; a newer copy is running; it's been up for more than a day ... Databases, Docker, and apps the OS launched are never flagged.
title: zombieports

claim: Users ask for LAN-exposure warnings: dev servers bound to 0.0.0.0 reachable 'from the cafe Wi-Fi' are flagged in zombieports ('open to your network'), Raycast Port Manager (orange exposure color), porthaven, and pier (LAN-reachability).
quote: open to your network when a dev server or database listens on all interfaces
title: zombieports

claim: Remote/SSH-host awareness is a requested edge: an HN user on Tailscale asked for customizable Docker URLs because localhost links don't open remote containers.
quote: Would be nice to have a flag to customize the URL displayed for Docker containers. I connect to my host via Tailscale, but I can't open links with localhost.
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Container visibility is a real feature request, not covered by naive port listing: a-grasso/portbook issue #4 (open) is 'Feature Request: Docker Container scanning network and ports'; stale Docker state causing wrong kills is sonar bug class #95-#98.
quote: Feature Request: Docker Container scanning network and ports
title: Feature Request: Docker Container scanning network and ports

claim: Worktree/parallel-checkout awareness is an emerging ask: sonar shipped 'ports per worktree' (#84) and has open #91 'Stop or kill a project together with all its checkouts'; a dev running ~a dozen Next.js devservers via Conductor worktrees can't map branch names to ports.
quote: I am not going to remember that 'fix-card-image-bg-loading' is running on port 3002 and 'test-dropbox-cache-bust' is running on port 3010.
title: Running a dozen Next.js devservers without losing your mind

claim: Port reservation/claiming is an emergent feature class: sonar added 'claims.ttl' (#109) and theekruger/portbook exists solely as 'a machine-wide port reservation registry' for humans+agents, built 'after an agent shuffled ports and silently killed another project's running servers'.
quote: Built after an agent shuffled ports and silently killed another project's running servers.
title: portbook

claim: Named localhost domains are a parallel solution users ask about: Portname/Local.vibe/portless map name.localhost to servers, and the one substantive comment asks 'Does it work with custom domains too? I've got a project that needs to test against a specific domain locally.'
quote: Does it work with custom domains too, or is it localhost only? I've got a project that needs to test against a specific domain locally.
title: Show HN: Portname - named localhost URLs for every dev server

claim: Counter-signal: a vocal HN minority sees the whole category as a shell-alias problem ('I just needed a simple alias', 'not sure why a whole cli app is needed', 'convenience tool... no need for it myself') - the differentiator that converts skeptics is context (project/framework/who-started/health), not listing.
quote: It looks to me like a convenience tool. Which is fine, but i see no need for it myself
title: Show HN: Sonar

claim: Port-conflict pain is large-scale and pre-dates these tools: the canonical StackOverflow 'port is already in use' question has ~494,623 views / score 297; Raycast's Port Manager extension alone reports 'more than 65,000 installs' (and 'works on Windows too').
quote: Port Manager has more than 65,000 installs.
title: Find and Kill the Process Using a Port on Mac

claim: Non-project background services break cwd-grouping - Ollama/LM Studio start with no project folder, so Rungeist ships manual port registration; user-defined labels/registration are needed for servers that grouping can't attribute.
quote: macOS starts Ollama and friends with no project folder, so anything that groups by folder never sees them. Add the port once and :11434 sits in the list like any other server
title: Rungeist

claim: Upstream dismissed the orphan problem: claude-code issue #62659 was 'closed as not planned' by a bot (per Sweepling's author), leaving third-party tray apps (Sweepling on Windows, cc-reaper on mac/linux) to fill the gap - an opening for a dashboard that detects and offers cleanup.
quote: There's an upstream issue about it, #62659, and a bot closed it as not planned.
title: Finding the processes Claude Code leaves running on Windows
